source.title: Mites of the family Bdellidae Dugès (Trombidiformes, Bdelloidea) from Saudi Arabia: a new species, new records, and a key to the world species of the genus Cyta von Heyden

where: Taxonomy, Cyta edafosa sp. nov., Description, Dorsum
quote: Prodorsum with two pairs of lateral eyes and a median unpaired eye; diameters of unpaired median eye 16 (15–17), anterior lateral eye 18 (17–20), and posterior lateral eye 19 (18–21); …
note: new trait for this paper: eye_diameter_mm (same key on main: Tapinocyba centralis desk-d363; no existing key records eye diameter in mm). The quote ends with a marked cut that drops the distance between the two lateral eyes, 49 (48–52), and 'with longitudinal striae in between'. Unit conversion: 16 µm = 0.016 mm (value as printed in µm, divided by 1000); printed range 15–17 µm. eye_diameter_mm is used because the sentence itself says 'diameters of'; neither the Methods nor the Description defines how an eye diameter is measured (the Methods define body length and width, setal length and leg length, all in micrometres).  The quote is the whole sentence from the Dorsum paragraph, which has the lowercase 'diameters' after a semicolon; the character after '(48–52)' is a comma, as printed. Preceding sentence: dorsal idiosoma covered in broken striae, with transverse striae between the at setae and longitudinal striae between the mps setae. Following sentence: 'Dorsal setae, other than smooth at and pt, faintly serrate.' The Diagnosis and Remarks do not mention eyes; the key couplet separates C. magdalenae 'Eyes absent' from 'Eyes present', with no eye numbers. The only new species in the paper; other taxa are new records or known species, with no eye measurements given. quote: Lateral ocelli pattern type 3A, with three small, similarly sized, lateral ocelli on each side of carapace; anterior and posterior situated in the same horizontal axis, median ocellus situated slightly below them; …
note: The quote ends with a marked cut that drops the last clause ('posterior ocellus situated one diameter apart from anterior and median ocelli.'), which gives the spacing only. It follows a separate sentence that opens 'Median ocular tubercle well developed, placed slightly in front of the middle of the carapace' and ends 'median ocelli medium large, ca. two diameters apart, and aiming laterally.' (the median ocelli there are described by size and spacing only; their number is not printed). The Diagnosis compares the species with B. negrei on pigmentation, metasomal stripes, androvestigia and metasomal granulation and gives no ocelli numbers; no difference in ocelli between the sexes is stated. Value 3 is per side, as the sentence says 'on each side of carapace'. The ocellar pattern 'type 3A' is the paper's term.
